patterns.name: House
patterns.notes: Textbook 4/4 house: offbeat open hat, clap on the backbeat, rim ghost lifting into the next bar.

patterns.name: Deep House
patterns.notes: Softer hats, one clap per bar, kick tuned long and round.

patterns.name: Tech House
patterns.notes: Sixteenth hats with a pushed kick on the last step.

patterns.name: Techno
patterns.notes: Deliberately strict — no bar-to-bar variation. Let the Tone knobs do the moving.

patterns.name: Hard Techno
patterns.notes: Everything accented, kick tuned short and clicky, snare slam into the turnaround.

patterns.name: Minimal
patterns.notes: Almost nothing. Space is the instrument.

patterns.name: Dub Techno
patterns.notes: Long, soft open hat as the only bright thing in the pattern.

patterns.name: Detroit Techno
patterns.notes: Stuttering hat figure, cymbal wash on the downbeat.

patterns.name: Acid Techno
patterns.notes: The classic 606-under-a-303 pattern. Global accent alternates strong/stronger.

patterns.name: Hardgroove
patterns.notes: Dense percussive layers with an accent lane in threes against the four.

patterns.name: Schranz
patterns.notes: Distorted-kick territory: double kick figure, cymbal on every beat.

patterns.name: Trance
patterns.notes: Big offbeat hat, rolling sixteenths, fills every fourth bar.

patterns.name: Hardcore
patterns.notes: Fast and blunt. Cymbal eighths give it the rave sheen.

patterns.name: EBM
patterns.notes: Eighth-note kick engine. Strict, because EBM does not swing.

patterns.name: Motorik
patterns.notes: Neu! pulse. Strict so it hypnotises.

patterns.name: Disco
patterns.notes: Open hat on every offbeat, clap on the backbeat, tom pickups.

patterns.name: Tresillo
patterns.notes: The 3-3-2 kick, straight. Clap on the backbeat so the displacement is audible against something fixed.

patterns.name: Tresillo Techno
patterns.notes: Same kick at techno tempo under relentless sixteenths. Every kick accented.

patterns.name: Half Tresillo
patterns.notes: The 3-3-2 stretched over the whole bar, so the kick lands three times and leaves room.

patterns.name: Dembow
patterns.notes: The boom-ch-boom-chick, with rim on the offbeats.

patterns.name: Baile Funk
patterns.notes: Tamborzão-flavoured tom answer under a bouncing kick.

patterns.name: Samba Electro
patterns.notes: Surdo-ish kick with a busy caixa-style snare.

patterns.name: Miami Bass
patterns.notes: 808-style bass pattern with clap doubling the snare.

patterns.name: Baltimore Club
patterns.notes: The Think-break bounce, stripped to a 606.

patterns.name: Footwork
patterns.notes: Triplet-feel kick against a straight rim sixteenth pulse.

patterns.name: Electro
patterns.notes: Syncopated electro kick, straight backbeat, eighth hats.

patterns.name: Big Beat
patterns.notes: Heavy, slightly slow, snare hit hard.

patterns.name: Broken Beat
patterns.notes: Everything slightly displaced — West London swing.

patterns.name: Industrial Techno
patterns.notes: Snare on the half-bar, kick limping slightly off the grid.

patterns.name: Ghetto House
patterns.notes: Offbeat claps, relentless hats.

patterns.name: Afro House
patterns.notes: Layered percussion in threes over a straight four.

patterns.name: Nu-Disco
patterns.notes: Disco frame, softer tone settings, stuttered hats.

patterns.name: Breakbeat
patterns.notes: Loose funk break skeleton, snare doing the talking.

patterns.name: Boom Bap
patterns.notes: Slow, dusty, flammed snare in the turnaround.

patterns.name: Trip-Hop
patterns.notes: Half-speed feel, snare dragged late in the bar.

patterns.name: Jungle
patterns.notes: Chopped-break placement at jungle tempo; sixteenth hats hold it together.

patterns.name: Drum & Bass
patterns.notes: Two-step: the whole point is the space between kick and snare.

patterns.name: Halftime
patterns.notes: Fast hats, half-time backbone. Huge and slow-feeling.

patterns.name: Funk Break
patterns.notes: Sixteenth-note hat shuffle under a busy snare.

patterns.name: Amen Feel
patterns.notes: Ghost-snare density approximating the classic break.

patterns.name: UK Garage
patterns.notes: Two-step garage with shuffle dialled in on CC18.

patterns.name: 606 Rock
patterns.notes: The original TR-606 Rock 1 idea, developed over four bars.

patterns.name: Post-Punk
patterns.notes: Driving and hard-hit, cymbal marking the half bars.

patterns.name: Coldwave
patterns.notes: Sparse, dry, a little sad.

patterns.name: Synth-Pop
patterns.notes: Clap doubling the snare — the 80s move.

patterns.name: Italo
patterns.notes: Tom answer phrase in the second half of each bar.

patterns.name: Freestyle
patterns.notes: Electro-latin freestyle kick with tom answers.

patterns.name: New Beat
patterns.notes: Slow, stiff, heavy. Belgian tempo.

patterns.name: Psy
patterns.notes: Rolling triplet-feel tom underneath a rigid kick. Strict on purpose.

patterns.name: Tribal Techno
patterns.notes: Toms carry the groove; the three-against-four rim keeps it rolling.

patterns.name: IDM Glitch
patterns.notes: Deliberately unstable. Rolls and flams used as glitches.

patterns.name: Braindance
patterns.notes: Warp-era wonk: displaced kick, chattering hats.

patterns.name: Cut-Up
patterns.notes: Fast, chopped, almost arrhythmic — but it loops.

patterns.name: Shoegaze Drive
patterns.notes: Washy cymbal every half bar, snare pushing sixteenths.

patterns.name: Noise Industrial
patterns.notes: All extremes on the nuance settings. Abrasive by design.

patterns.name: 16th Shuffle
patterns.notes: Shuffle amount pushed past half — swung sixteenths.

patterns.name: Swung Boom Bap
patterns.notes: Heavy swing plus flams — the drunkest pattern in the bank.

patterns.name: Reggaeton
patterns.notes: Clap doubling the dembow snare for weight.

patterns.name: 6/8 Feel
patterns.notes: Twelve-feel bell pattern mapped onto the 16-step grid.

patterns.name: Cumbia Machine
patterns.notes: Cumbia's limping guiro figure translated to rim and tom.

patterns.name: Bossa Electro
patterns.notes: Clave-like rim over a soft two-feel. Strict to keep it polite.

patterns.name: Boogie
patterns.notes: Slinky early-80s kick with a touch of shuffle.

patterns.name: Polyrhythm 5
patterns.notes: Rim in fives, tom in sevens, kick in fours. Phases across the 64 steps.

patterns.name: Drone Pulse
patterns.notes: Slowest pattern in the bank. Meant to sit under a long drone.
